newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU refers German energy mergers to national body.
newsitem.headline: EU refers German energy mergers to national body.

text.p: The European Commission said on Tuesday it had referred a plan by RWE Energy AG to take a 50 percent stake in Thyssengas GmbH to the German bundeskartelamt competition authority.
It said it had also referred to the German cartel office a related plan by Bayernwerk AG to acquire RWE's share in Isarwerke GmbH.
It said the Bundeskartelamt had requested the referral "because of the threat of the strengthening of dominant positions in regional gas and electricity markets."

The Commission said in a statement that both of the deals fell under EU merger rules but IT had decided to refer the case to German officials under provisions that allow member states to investigate if there is a threat of cresating or strengthening a dominant position within their territory.

"Although initiatives are being taken to liberalise the energy markets on the European and German levels, the electricity and gas markets in Germany are still currently characterised by a system of geographic monopolies," it said.
